instantiated_cells.justification: Lobbying 'as a lobbyist' is prohibited unless the person is licensed and authorized (§13.66), and a 'lobbyist' is a paid/compensated individual whose duties include lobbying (§13.62(11)), with only a limited ≤$500 verified-statement exemption from licensing/registration/reporting (§13.621(5)).
A lobbyist license 'shall expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year,' requiring renewal every 24 months.
Lobbyists file a license application (§13.63) while principals file a separate registration statement (§13.64), making them independent registrants with separate filings.
The lobbyist license application must include items like the applicant’s social security number (or alternative statement) and signature, but no photograph requirement is stated.
Public officials and legislative employees are not subject to key lobbying provisions when acting in an official capacity under the 'Performance of public official duties' exemption.
An agency that files a statement under §13.695 and named officials are exempt from multiple lobbying provisions (§13.621(2)), instead subject to the separate agency statement regime in §13.695.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled provisions specify change-notification deadlines for agencies under §13.695(2) but do not state a general lobbyist license/registration change-update deadline for lobbyists; any such requirement would need additional sections not provided.

Wisconsin requires a lobbyist to be licensed and authorized before engaging in lobbying (§13.66), but the statute text provided does not specify a numeric 'days after first lobbying' deadline for the lobbyist to register/license, so an integer day count cannot be derived.
